RUN STATE after the s1o collision (orchestrate-epic, 2026-09-03 17:53). The epic is idle by choice, waiting on an external merge. No park, no escalation, nothing needed from Manuel right now.

Sequence: Manuel approved pulling ancora-s1o in as the epic's prerequisite. My mistake, recorded so the next run does not repeat it: I read the ticket, then spent about thirteen minutes on worktree setup, rigor and boundary checks, and prompt rendering, then spawned without re-reading. Ticket admission step 9 puts the start immediately before the spawn precisely so state gets re-checked there. A single bw-marker latest call at that moment would have returned IMPLEMENTED and stopped the spawn. Adding to LESSONS.

Both ancora-s1o and ancora-p47 are ceded to the ship session's PR against main and remain children of this epic, in_progress, not driven from here. The suite fix is 35372ed, read and judged sound independently, with ten consecutive green full-suite runs reported at 31 to 59 seconds against the 210 seconds this epic measured.

The other fourteen children stay blocked behind ancora-s1o, which is the correct state: the epic worktree /Users/mz/src/ancora-xla sits at 5d9cb40, and every child records that as its admission base. When the ship PR merges, the work is to rebase the epic branch onto the new main, update the Base: line and the recorded base in each child, close ancora-s1o and ancora-p47 against the merge, and admit the first real wave. Building on their unmerged branch instead would be fragile and is deliberately not being done.

CORRECTION to the rebase plan in my previous comment (2026-09-03 18:02). I wrote that the post-merge work includes updating the recorded base in each child. That is wrong and would do damage if followed literally.

None carries a literal base sha as its admission base; every Verification and Merge gate section says 'the epic base sha recorded at admission' as a phrase, which is deliberate and stays correct across a rebase. - ancora-sfu twice, describing how the squash destroyed two Spec-Ack trailers and produced the 31 change/uncovered_file warnings, and a status note about the stale trunk-is-red framing.
- ancora-xla.5 once, in F30b, citing that spec.check --base 5d9cb40 passes because that is what github.event.before would have been for the post-merge push.

Rewriting any of those to a new sha would break the account they give. Leave them.

So the post-merge work is smaller than I said: rebase /Users/mz/src/ancora-xla onto the new main, update only the epic description's Base: line, close ancora-s1o and ancora-p47 against the merge sha, and admit the first wave. No per-child edits.

PR #2 verified independently before acting on it: gh reports it MERGED at 18:17:07Z as squash commit 7511407, and the merged diff carries both children's content (lib/ancora/change_analysis.ex, lib/ancora/gate.ex, 42 new lines in test/ancora/gate_test.exs, and the per-module build path in test/support/ancora_case.exs). Not adopted into this epic: ancora-ufm, filed by the ship session's auditor. LESSONS
- [other] A cost a grader calls affordable must be measured under repetition, not at one sample. The per-call build copy was reviewed, priced at one sample, waved through, and then failed the suite about one run in three. (from ancora-s1o)
- [other] Re-read the ticket's latest state in the same breath as acting on it. Minutes of setup can sit between reading and acting, and another session can finish the work in that window. (from ancora-s1o)
- [other] When you cite a before-and-after measurement, name exactly which two trees you compared. An audit caught a cold verifier accepting a comparison of a branch off main against main, which was vacuous. (from ancora-p47)
- [stale-spec] A ticket that changes a rule must be allowed to edit EVERY spec that states the old rule, not only the spec of its own Advances subject. Withholding one forces the worker to choose between a scope violation and shipping a corpus that contradicts itself, and it will choose silently. Three tickets have now hit this: ancora-xla.2, ancora-v1n, and by inspection ancora-11w and ancora-sfu will too. (from ancora-v1n)
- [untested-clause] Retagging a test onto a new requirement can silently orphan the clause it used to prove. The gate stays quiet because the old requirement still has other tagged tests, so requirement_unverified never fires. Check clause coverage by hand when tags move. (from ancora-v1n)
- [other] A green gate is not proof of a consistent corpus. ancora-v1n passes spec.check while shipping two scenarios that predict opposite outcomes from identical input, because nothing in the gate compares requirements across subjects. (from ancora-v1n)

PREEMPTIVE FIX applied to every remaining child (orchestrator, 2026-09-03 19:15). The ancora-v1n verification exposed a defect in how I wrote these tickets, and rather than let it bounce ticket after ticket I audited all fourteen and fixed it in one pass.

The defect: a ticket's Allowed touches permitted a production file while withholding the subject spec that governs it. Under ancora's own rules, editing that file raises drift that ONLY a substantive edit to that spec can clear, so the worker is left choosing between a mechanical scope violation and shipping a corpus that contradicts itself. ancora-v1n chose silently, retagging two tests onto a new requirement and inverting them, which left a clause in ancora.gate.two_append_guards both untrue and covered by no test, while the gate stayed quiet because that requirement kept five other tagged tests.

Method, so this is checkable rather than asserted: I parsed the Modules line at the head of each of the seven subject specs, derived the lib path for every module, and cross-checked each ticket's Allowed lib files against the specs it lists. Seven of eleven not-yet-started children had at least one gap.

- ancora-gqb: permits lib/ancora/derive files, missing ancora.derive
- ancora-n24: permits lib/ancora/append_only.ex, missing ancora.gate
- ancora-11w: permits lib/ancora/git.ex and lib/ancora/trailer.ex, missing ancora.derive and ancora.findings
- ancora-sfu: missing ancora.derive, ancora.findings, ancora.tasks
- ancora-xla.1: eleven lib files, missing ancora.derive, ancora.gate, ancora.review, ancora.tasks
- ancora-xla.6: nineteen lib files, missing ancora.derive, ancora.findings, ancora.parsing
- ancora-xla.8: missing ancora.derive

Each addition names the specific permitted file that triggers it, and is constrained to acknowledgment edits for that ticket's own changes, never weakening a must and never deleting a requirement. This is not blanket permission to rewrite other subjects.

Separately, every one of the fourteen children now carries this clause, including the three in flight: any spec whose stated rule the ticket's change makes false may be corrected in the same diff, and doing so is expected rather than tolerated. That is the rule ancora-v1n needed and did not have. A worker that finds it has falsified a requirement should now fix it and say so, instead of routing around it.

Four children needed no spec additions and already listed what they touch: ancora-xla.3, ancora-xla.5, ancora-xla.7, ancora-xla.9.

Honest note on cost: this is seven bounces that would probably have happened one at a time, each burning an implementation attempt and a grader pair. It is also seven chances to ship a self-contradicting corpus from a project whose entire product is a spec gate. Finding it took one cold verification that I did not want to hear.

GRADING LADDER RESULTS, first three tickets (orchestrator, 2026-09-03 19:25). Both cold verifications failed, both catches are real, and neither was visible to any automated check in this repository.

ancora-v1n: VERIFY FAIL, then AUDIT BOUNCE to implementer. The audit did not inherit the verifier's finding; it re-derived the counts, confirmed all three gaps, and found the verifier UNDER-read one of them. Not only did the 'or its subject id' clause lose its test, all four authorization tests moved to the parsing tag, so the entire suppression half of ancora.gate.two_append_guards now has zero tests under its own id while five other tagged tests keep spec/requirement_unverified silent. Remedy is three specified edits: delete the false clause from the requirement statement, correct the contradicted scenario's given, and dual-tag two tests using the list form the tag scanner already supports. Respawned as attempt 2 of 2 with the audit comment verbatim; the widened Allowed touches mean the remedy is now legal, which it was not on attempt 1. Bounce count 1.

ancora-xla.2: VERIFY FAIL, now in audit. Two gaps. The serious one is a REGRESSION in a ticket whose entire purpose is eliminating verdict-less crashes: an unreadable test file used to produce a clean tags/parse_error finding and a proper tier=branch verdict, and now produces empty stdout and a RuntimeError on stderr. The verifier traced the mechanism precisely, that a with's else never sees its own body's return value, so gate_error/1 is unreachable from the four converted sites, and reproduced it against a scratch fixture at both trees. The spec clause promising env-tier handling of unreadable inputs is therefore written but not implemented.

The second gap is the one I asked it to check specifically, and it paid off. The implementer claimed a close path went from 500.7 ms to 14.7 ms. The verifier re-measured 20 samples per scenario across two named trees and found the opposite: base 0.02 to 0.08 ms against head 10.58 to 10.77 ms. Every head sample sits just above the 10 ms bound, because Port.close/1 terminates synchronously and never delivers an exit status, so the wait the new spec clause describes can never succeed. The call got roughly 300x slower and the clause is vacuous. That is exactly the vacuous-comparison failure mode the ship session's auditor caught this morning, caught again, this time before it merged.

ancora-xla.4 is still in cold verification, with the browser assertion in its hands.

Grader tally so far: 3 cold verifications, 2 audits, 1 bounce, 0 escalations. Two of three verified tickets came back FAIL, and in both cases the implementation was substantially correct with a specific hole. That ratio is the ladder working, not workers underperforming.

LESSONS
- [other] A cost a grader calls affordable must be measured under repetition, not at one sample. (from ancora-s1o)
- [other] Re-read the ticket's latest state in the same breath as acting on it. (from ancora-s1o)
- [other] When you cite a before-and-after measurement, name which two trees you compared, and be certain it reproduces. Two claims have now failed this: one vacuous comparison of a branch off main against main, and one 34x speedup that re-measured as a 300x slowdown. (from ancora-p47, ancora-xla.2)
- [stale-spec] A ticket that changes a rule must correct every spec that states the old rule, in the same diff. Every child's Allowed touches now permits that explicitly. (from ancora-v1n)
- [untested-clause] Moving a @tag from one requirement to another can silently orphan everything the old requirement proved. spec/requirement_unverified stays quiet as long as any other tagged test remains. (from ancora-v1n)
- [other] A green gate proves neither a consistent corpus nor a true spec clause. Two tickets have now added spec sentences describing behaviour the code does not implement, and the gate passed both. Write the clause to match what you built. (from ancora-v1n, ancora-xla.2)

ADMISSION DEFECT, third instance, and the sweep that closes it (orchestrator, 2026-09-03 19:40).

The ancora-xla.4 verifier found the same class of defect a third time, in a new flavour, and this one is structurally guaranteed rather than merely likely. Ancora.PolicyFiles.missing_decision?/1 at lib/ancora/policy_files.ex:115 fires change/missing_decision whenever any path under .spec/specs/ changes without an accompanying decision-record change in the SAME diff. Every child of this epic is required to edit a spec. Eight of fourteen permitted that edit while withholding .spec/decisions/**, so every one of them would have hit a forced finding with no legal way to clear it: ancora-11w, ancora-xla.1, ancora-xla.3, ancora-xla.4, ancora-xla.5, ancora-xla.6, ancora-xla.7, ancora-xla.8. All eight fixed, with a warning in the text not to write a hollow decision line to silence the finding, since a grader will read that as finding-silencing and bounce it.

The three instances of one root cause, stated plainly because I keep making it: I wrote Allowed lists that permit an action while withholding what that action structurally forces.
1. Permitting a source file while withholding the subject spec that governs it. Seven tickets.
2. Withholding a spec that states a rule the ticket's change falsifies. All fourteen now carry an explicit clause.
3. Permitting a spec edit while withholding the decision record that edit forces. Eight tickets.

Every one of these was found by a grader rather than by me, and each was found only because the grader checked a mechanism rather than accepting a claim. The xla.4 verifier did not take the implementer's word that the decision edit was forced; it read PolicyFiles and proved it.

Ticket routing this round:
- ancora-v1n came back IMPLEMENTED on attempt 2 with all three ordered edits present, a 13-line delta across 2 files, and no scope creep. In delta-scoped re-verification now, with instructions to sweep the whole corpus for any THIRD site still claiming subject-scope authorization, and to judge whether the dual-tagging actually restores coverage or merely satisfies the gate.
- ancora-xla.4 returned VERIFY PASS with a genuinely non-vacuous proof. Selective Audit Gate applied: every condition holds except the Elixir test-quality one, since the diff makes assertional edits to review_test.exs and carries no test-critic record. That is a missing condition, not a satisfied one, so the test critic is running rather than the gate being waved through.
- ancora-xla.2 remains in audit.

Filed standalone, deliberately not adopted into this epic: ancora-i19, Prism now ships inert in every review artifact. Zero elements carry a language class after ancora-xla.4, so roughly 60K of grammars and CSS render for nothing while ancora.review.prism_carried still requires it be carried. Two honest options, decision needed: give Prism real work, or retire the requirement and drop the assets. The second matches this epic's governing principle. Retiring it depends on ancora-n24's retirement vocabulary or an ADR under ancora-v1n's rule. Manuel's call whether it joins this epic.

Grader tally: 4 cold verifications, 2 audits, 1 test-critic running, 1 bounce, 0 escalations. Three of four verifications found something real.

AUDIT 2 RESULT and routing (orchestrator, 2026-09-03 19:50).

ancora-xla.2: AUDIT BOUNCE to implementer, attempt 2 of 2 now running. The auditor did not inherit the verifier's evidence. It read the control flow itself, built its own scratch fixture, reproduced both gaps at both commits, and took its own 20-sample measurement. Its numbers: close/1 mean 0.126 ms at base against 11.584 ms at HEAD, every HEAD sample at or above the 10 ms bound. Two independent measurements now contradict the implementer's claimed 500.7 ms to 14.7 ms improvement, in the opposite direction. That claim is being withdrawn from the record as part of the remedy.

Its remedy is worth noting for how it was scoped. Gap 1 is a code fix and the spec clause stays as written, because the clause is correct and the code is what fails to reach it. Gap 2 is the reverse: the spec sentence goes, because Port.close/1 cannot deliver the message the sentence describes, and the recommended code change is a REVERT to the monitor form that was there at 7511407 rather than any new mechanism. The auditor wrote, in as many words, no memo, no registry, no new process, no new module. That is the epic's governing principle being applied by a grader without being asked, which is the outcome that principle was recorded for.

The regression itself deserves stating plainly, because it is the sharpest example so far of why a green gate proves nothing on its own. An unreadable tagged test file at 7511407 produced a clean tags/parse_error finding and a proper result=fail tier=branch verdict. At c3aaa97 it produces completely empty stdout and a RuntimeError on stderr, which is the precise defect signature this ticket was written to eliminate. mix spec.check --base 7511407 ends result=pass on that same commit.

Both bounced tickets are now on their final implementation attempt. A third bounce on either escalates to Manuel rather than returning to a worker. Per-ticket bounce counts are 1 of 2 on ancora-v1n and 1 of 2 on ancora-xla.2; no mechanical-remedy bounces have been used on either.

Host load is 96 on ten cores, so ancora-xla.2's retry is the only implementer running and nothing new is being admitted. Also live: the delta-scoped re-verification of ancora-v1n and the Elixir test critic on ancora-xla.4.

Running tally: 4 cold verifications, 2 audits, 2 bounces, 1 test critic, 0 escalations. Three of four verifications found something real, and both audits upheld the verifier they were checking. No audit has yet routed to a verifier, which means no verifier in this epic has been wrong.

Where each in-flight child stands, and the exact next action for each:

Resume by spawning the test critic against 7511407..420fb94 in /Users/mz/src/ancora-xla.2, then re-applying the gate. If it passes, this merges. Bounce 1 of 2.

The work order is four edits, fully specified and pre-measured by the auditor, all in test files, nothing under lib/.

RESUMED (orchestrator, 2026-09-03 20:45). Five things live.

Base correction applied at admission, and it matters. The epic HEAD moved to b717ba4 when ancora-xla.4 merged, so new stage worktrees now branch from b717ba4 rather than 7511407. ancora-gqb was admitted on that basis and its prompt says so explicitly, because it edits lib/ancora/review/html.ex and the merged sibling just changed that file. Branching a new child off the original base would have handed it a tree without its sibling's work and guaranteed a conflict. The 'epic base sha recorded at admission' phrasing in every ticket is what makes this safe: it now means 7511407 for the three children admitted earlier and b717ba4 for gqb, which is correct, and it is why literal shas were kept out of the ticket text.

Live now:
- ancora-v1n, implementer attempt 3 of 3. The audit's four-edit order rendered verbatim, all in test files, nothing under lib/. A third bounce escalates to Manuel rather than returning to a worker.
- ancora-xla.2, elixir-test-critic. This is the one condition its selective audit gate is short of. If it passes, the ticket merges.
- ancora-xla.8, cold verifier. It is being told to prove the scaffold renames BY EXECUTION rather than by reading the diff: actually run mix spec.init into a scratch directory and confirm nothing ships literal EEx syntax, since a rename plus a copy path is exactly the change that silently writes <%= ... %> into a user's repository. It is also told to recompute vendored digests itself rather than trusting pinned values, and to check that the two-line traversal-safety comment on base_view.ex states a property the code actually has, since a false comment about traversal safety is worse than none.

Deliberately NOT admitted despite an idle machine: ancora-xla.7, ancora-xla.1, ancora-xla.3, ancora-xla.5, ancora-xla.6, ancora-xla.9, ancora-sfu. Every one of them edits .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md, ancora.tasks.spec.md or ancora.derive.spec.md, and ancora-xla.2 and ancora-xla.8 already conflict with each other on four files including ancora.derive.spec.md while both sit unmerged. Two tickets adding clauses to the same requirement block is a real conflict, which a rebase worker refuses rather than resolves. Starting six more of those now would build rebase debt on the spec corpus, which is precisely the churn this project exists to reduce. They admit once the two pending children merge and collapse the conflict surface.

That is a judgement call, so it is stated rather than buried: an idle machine is not on its own a reason to start work whose cost lands later, in conflicts, on a corpus that is this repository's actual product.

GRADER DISCIPLINE DEFECT, caught by the rebase worker (orchestrator, 2026-09-03 21:20). Recording it because it nearly corrupted a merge and because it is mine to fix, not the worker's.

The rebase worker for ancora-xla.2 refused to start: /Users/mz/src/ancora-xla.2 had a dirty tree, which is an explicit stop condition, and rebasing over uncommitted work would have been the wrong move. It stopped, reported precisely what it found, and touched nothing. That is exactly right and it is worth saying so, because the easy failure here would have been to rebase anyway and lose the difference silently.

Diagnosis: test/support/tmp_git_repo.exs was MM, modified in both index and working tree. HEAD and the working tree both carried 6570549, the poll version this ticket added. The INDEX alone carried aa9c3fa, which is byte-identical to 7511407's version of that file. So only the index was stale and it held nothing not already in git history.

Origin: the Elixir test critic that ran on ancora-xla.2 immediately before. It measured the cleanup regression by restoring the base version of that exact file and counting 'fatal: not a git repository' occurrences across three runs each way, which is good methodology and produced a real finding. But restoring a file with git writes to BOTH the index and the working tree, and it put back only the working tree. Its report described comparing 'a copied tree', which is not what the index shows.

Cleared with git reset HEAD on that path, which unstages without touching the working tree. Tree is clean, HEAD is still 420fb94, git diff HEAD is empty, nothing lost. The rebase worker has been told to resume from step 2.

My defect, not the critic's: I told it 'read-only, do not edit any file' and then asked it questions it could only answer by mutating and restoring. Those instructions are in tension, and the critic chose the answer over the letter, which was the better call. The fix is to say what I actually mean.

LESSONS
- [fixture-leak] A grader that measures by mutation must restore the INDEX as well as the working tree, and confirm with git status --porcelain before reporting. Restoring a file from another revision stages it; putting the working copy back does not unstage it. Two graders in this epic have now mutated a tree to measure, and one left the index dirty, which stopped a merge.
- [other] When instructing a read-only grader, say 'you may mutate to measure, and you must restore and prove the tree is clean' rather than 'do not edit any file'. The second forbids the technique that produced the epic's best findings, so a good grader will ignore it and a bad one will skip the measurement.
- [other] A worker that refuses to proceed on a precondition and reports precisely is doing its job. The rebase worker here prevented a silent loss.

SECURITY FINDING, confirmed and filed (orchestrator, 2026-09-03 22:10). This is the most important thing this epic has produced and it was not on anyone's list.

ancora-kzw, P0, labelled security, filed standalone: a hostile git tree escapes the base-view write root. Ancora.BaseView.materialize writes every blob using the path git reports verbatim. A tree entry can be literally named '..'. git mktree accepts it, ls-tree -r emits the joined path, git resolves it on read, Path.join leaves it in place, and the kernel resolves it at File.write! so the file lands outside the temp root at attacker-chosen depth. The escaped file also survives the File.rm_rf cleanup at gate.ex:67 and review.ex:41, because it was never inside the root.

This matters because ancora is a gate that runs against repositories its operator does not control.

I was WRONG about this and the record should show it. When the ancora-xla.8 verifier reported it, I tried to reproduce, could not, and wrote a note saying so: git refused the path shape that would escape, and the shape it accepted joined back to a directory where the write fails. I explicitly declined to report a vulnerability to Manuel on evidence I could not confirm, and routed it to audit naming the three-level shape as the candidate I had not built. That was the right process and the wrong conclusion.

The auditor built exactly that shape and it works. Nest 'a' then '..' then '..' around a blob, and ls-tree emits 'a/../../evil.txt'. I then reproduced it a third time myself before filing: git returns the blob for that path with exit 0, and the join expands one directory above the root. The mechanism explains both of my earlier observations and is worth recording because it will mislead the next reader too: git normalises a rev:path string ONLY when the path starts with './' or '../', which is what produces 'outside repository'. Anything else is a literal component walk against tree entry NAMES, so an embedded '..' matches an entry named '..'. A two-level probe therefore finds nothing and looks conclusive.

Confirmed from both sides: '<rev>:../evil.txt' is refused; '<rev>:a/./../../evil.txt' fails for want of an entry named '.'; '<rev>:a/../../evil.txt' succeeds. The auditor also confirmed both read paths are affected, batch port and fallback alike.

Three agents reproduced it independently before it was written down as fact. That is the standard this epic has been holding and it is why the report is trustworthy.

ancora-xla.8 is bounced for the COMMENT ONLY, bounce 1 of 2. Its two-line comment asserts the defence that does not exist, which is worse than no comment because it tells the next reader not to look on the exact line where they otherwise would. Its Allowed touches permit that file for a comment only, so the real fix cannot land there and must not be attempted; the prompt says so explicitly. Everything else in that diff stands.

Also merged since the last note: ancora-xla.2 closed at 52b4536, merge gate green at 344 tests. ancora-v1n is approved and rebasing onto that new tip; three files were changed by both it and the epic, including ancora.gate.spec.md which two tickets have now edited for different reasons, so its rebase worker is told to refuse any spec conflict rather than resolve it and to treat the spec gate as the real check, because two individually valid edits can be jointly inconsistent in a way a clean rebase hides.

Tally: 4 of 16 closed after ancora-v1n lands, 7 cold verifications, 4 audits, 2 test critics, 2 rebase workers, 4 bounces, 0 escalations, 1 security finding.
